evals.query: I just created a Next.js app with the App Router (npx create-next-app@latest my-project --typescript --eslint --app). Add Tailwind CSS v4 to it. Give me the exact install command, every file to create or edit, and their contents.
expected_behavior: Installs tailwindcss, @tailwindcss/postcss and postcss, not @tailwindcss/vite
Creates postcss.config.mjs with plugins: { "@tailwindcss/postcss": {} } as the only plugin, without autoprefixer or postcss-import
Puts @import "tailwindcss"; in app/globals.css instead of @tailwind base/components/utilities
Does not create a tailwind.config.js and does not add a content array
Does not run npx tailwindcss init

evals.query:
In my Tailwind v4 Vite project, add a brand color called midnight (#121063) usable as bg-midnight and text-midnight, and make Oswald (loaded from Google Fonts) available as font-display. Here is my current src/app.css:

@import "tailwindcss";
expected_behavior: Declares --color-midnight: #121063 inside an @theme block, not in tailwind.config.js and not only on :root
Declares --font-display with Oswald inside @theme
Places the Google Fonts @import url(...) above @import "tailwindcss"
Does not wipe the default palette unless asked (no --color-*: initial)
Uses bg-midnight, text-midnight and font-display in the example markup

evals.query: Build a dark mode toggle for my Tailwind v4 site. The user picks light, dark or system, the choice is saved in localStorage, and dark styles must apply when <html> has the class dark. Show the CSS and the JavaScript, and avoid a flash of the wrong theme on load.
expected_behavior: Adds @custom-variant dark (&:where(.dark, .dark *)); in the CSS instead of darkMode: 'class' in a JS config
Runs an inline script in <head> that toggles the dark class from localStorage.theme and window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)")
Uses localStorage.removeItem("theme") for the system option
Styles elements with dark: variants such as dark:bg-gray-800
Recommends running npx @tailwindcss/upgrade in a new branch and reviewing the diff
Replaces the PostCSS config with @tailwindcss/postcss alone and drops autoprefixer
Replaces the @tailwind directives with @import "tailwindcss";
Moves the brand color to @theme as --color-brand and the dark mode setting to @custom-variant dark (&:where(.dark, .dark *));
Replaces safelist with @source inline("bg-red-500");
Renames shadow-sm to shadow-xs, rounded to rounded-sm, flex-shrink-0 to shrink-0 and focus:outline-none to focus:outline-hidden
Replaces bg-white bg-opacity-50 with bg-white/50
Adds an explicit border color because v4 borders default to currentColor
Rewrites ring as ring-3 with an explicit ring color such as ring-blue-500 to keep the v3 look

evals.query:
In a SvelteKit app using Tailwind v4, this component style block fails with an error that bg-brand is an unknown utility, although bg-brand works in markup:

<style>
  .card { @apply bg-brand rounded-lg; }
</style>

Fix it.
expected_behavior: Explains that a component <style> block is compiled separately and does not see the theme
Adds @reference pointing to the main stylesheet (for example @reference "../app.css";) at the top of the style block
Offers the faster alternative of using the CSS variable directly, for example background-color: var(--color-brand)
Does not suggest adding the class to a safelist or a tailwind.config.js

evals.query: My React component builds Tailwind classes like className={`bg-${color}-600 hover:bg-${color}-500`} and the colors never show up in production. Why, and how do I fix it in Tailwind v4?
expected_behavior: Explains that Tailwind scans source files as plain text and only generates complete class names it finds
Maps each prop value to a full class string such as { blue: "bg-blue-600 hover:bg-blue-500" }
Mentions @source inline(...) as the v4 way to safelist classes if a mapping is impossible, not the v3 safelist option

evals.query: Write a plain CSS card component (no framework, no build step) with a subtle shadow, rounded corners and a hover lift effect. Just give me the HTML and a <style> block.
expected_behavior: Does not load the tailwindcss-docs skill or its references
Answers with plain CSS properties (box-shadow, border-radius, transform, transition), without Tailwind classes or directives
Rewrites bg-[--brand] as bg-(--brand)
Moves the important modifier to the end: font-bold!
Replaces the @layer utilities block with @utility content-auto { content-visibility: auto; } so variants work on it
Replaces focus:outline-none with focus:outline-hidden
Adds an explicit border color because v4 borders default to currentColor
